scope: Publisher-owned draft instructional lesson; teacher review and institutional publication required before students see it.
title: Week 2 · Multi-Step Equations and Literal Formulas

lessons.title: Week 2 · Day 5 · Demonstrate, Explain, and Revise
lessons.body:
ALGEBRA I • UNIT 1 • WEEK 2 • DAY 5 OF 5
WARM-UP · FIND THE FIRST INVALID STEP (5 min)
A student solves (x+3)/2 = (2x−1)/3 by multiplying only the left side by 6. Explain which equality property is violated and rewrite the first transformation correctly. Do not solve the equation yet.

STRATEGY REVIEW (10 min)
Before the checkpoint: (1) read the entire original expression and note any nonzero denominator restriction; (2) apply the same valid operation to both sides; (3) distribute and collect like terms carefully; (4) classify identities or contradictions; (5) substitute back into the original equation; (6) for word problems, specify units and feasible whole-number constraints. FORMULA EXAMPLE. A = (1/2)bh, with b ≠ 0, yields h = 2A/b. Check a sample triangle: A=12 cm², b=6 cm, h=4 cm. Always carry units when interpreting, but do not assume an answer without evidence.

COLLABORATIVE CRITIQUE (10 min)
In pairs, compare two solutions to 4(x−2)=2x+6: one correctly gives x=7, while one incorrectly distributes 4(x−2) as 4x−2. Name the first invalid step, repair it, and substitute the correct answer. Then discuss why 2(x+3)=2x+6 describes every real x, while 2(x+3)=2x+7 has no solution.

INDEPENDENT FORMATIVE CHECKPOINT (20 min)
Work alone and show all reasoning. 1. Solve (x−1)/3=(2x+1)/5. 2. Solve 3(2x−4)=4x+10, and check. 3. Classify 5(x+2)−3=5x+7; justify one, none, or infinitely many. 4. Solve F=(9/5)C+32 for C, and state any nonzero restrictions if you divide by a symbol. 5. Solve A=(1/2)bh for b when h≠0. 6. A school orders 7 supplies per learner plus 21 shared supplies, using 105 total. Find learners, with units. 7. A bus seats 18 students; 50 students need transport. Express the minimum number of buses with an inequality and explain your rounding. 8. A peer changes x/3+4=9 to x+4=27 when multiplying by 3. Explain and fix the mistake. Do not use a calculator to replace written reasoning.

REFLECTION AND NEXT ACTION (10 min)
Choose one checkpoint solution and explain how you verified it against the original equation or constraint. Name one error you corrected today and one remaining question. Submit your work for teacher review; the teacher will score and release feedback. If you need a revision, follow the teacher's returned-work instructions.
learningTargets: I can independently solve rational and multi-step linear equations with equality-preserving steps.
I can rearrange a literal formula and state any nonzero restrictions.
I can model a contextual constraint and use evidence to correct a mistake.
